BENGALURU (SCCH-24), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

Both claimants as well as the insurer are in appeals challenging the award of Rs.22,35,000/-
awarded for the death of Sangram, first year MBBS Student.

2. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 29.11.2014,
Sangram, a 18 year old died.
3. It is not also in dispute that the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.

4. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident which has resulted in the death of Sangram.

The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 21,60,000  2. Loss of love and affection 50,000  3.
Transportation expenses 10,000  Funeral and obsequies  4. 15,000  ceremony expenses  Total 22,35,000 5.
The insurer contends that the assessment of the monthly income of Rs.20,000/- is on the higher side while the claimant contends that the assessment of Rs.20,000/- per month was inadequate.

Hanumanthappa vs Reliance General Insurance Company ... on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143248972/
4 6.

sentences.text: The fact that the deceased had secured a seat on merit and was a student of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya at Yadagiri School is not in dispute.

In my view, having regard to the further fact that the deceased had secured a MBBS seat on merit, interest of justice would be served if the monthly income of the deceased is determined as Rs.30,000/-.
7. Since the deceased was aged 18 years, 40% is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.42,000/-.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and then, his monthly income would be Rs.21,000/-.

8. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.21,000/-
9.
As the deceased was aged 18 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.45,36,000/- (Rs.21,000 x 12 x 18 ) towards "loss of dependency".
10.

The claimants being the parents and siblings, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,76,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

11. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 45,36,000  2. Loss of Consortium 1,76,000  3. Conventional Heads 33,000  Total 47,45,000 12.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.47,45,000/- as against Rs.22,35,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
13.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

16. The appeal of the insurer is dismissed and the appeal of the claimants is accordingly allowed in part.
17. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
18. The claimants would not be entitled for the interest on the compensation for the delayed period of 443 days in filing the appeal.
